liebermann.laws: ECf, Lib Lond, Leis Wl, CHn cor, In Cn, Wl art
liebermann.notes: Parchment, ff. 4–104 c. 1325; in the starred pieces it derives with Pl from a common exemplar sp. Contains Glanvill, ECf (with rubrics from ECf retr), Libertas Londoniensis, the Latin Leis Willelme from L, Henry I's coronation charter, 13th-century laws, Registrum brevium, De longitudine Anglie, Instituta Cnuti, Huntingdon's 'Chnutus rex' (placing S in the Ip Hunt class) and from the Tripartita Wl art and the Genealogia Normannica continued to John. S was copied in Vl and Harley 785.

entries.text_de:
British Museum Harley 746, Perg., f. 4—104 um 13252. In den hier besternten Stücken fliesst S mit Pl, laut gleicher Fehler und gleicher Reihenfolge in f. 49—55, 77—85, aus Einer Vorlage sp.

F. 4—48 *Glanvilla; f. 48b leer; f. 49 *ECf, u. S. 627, Rubren aus ECf retr; f. 54b *Lib Lond, u. S. 673; f. 55b Leis Wl Lat aus L, u. S. 493; f. 59 CHn cor (vgl. u. West), u. S. 521; f. 59v.—69 Gesetze 13. Jhs.; f. 70 Registrum brevium; f. 75 Heptarchie, Bischofsitze, polit. Bezirke *De longitudine . . Anglie.

F. 77 *In Cn, u. S. 612; f. 84 *Chnutus rex cum XX annis, d. i. Huntingdon3, wodurch auch S zur Classe Ip Hunt (o. S. xxxi) sich einordnet. Es folgt aus Tripartita: f. 84 *Wl art, u. S. 486; f. 84b *Geneal. Normannica usque II Henricum, fortgesetzt bis Johann.

F. 86b leer; f. 87—98b Gesetze 13. Jhs.

S ward copirt in Vl und Harley 785.
entries.text_en:
British Museum Harley 746, parchment, f. 4—104 c. 13252. In the pieces starred here S derives together with Pl — on the evidence of identical errors and identical order in f. 49—55, 77—85 — from a single exemplar, sp.

F. 4—48 *Glanvilla; f. 48b blank; f. 49 *ECf, below, p. 627, rubrics from ECf retr; f. 54b *Lib Lond, below, p. 673; f. 55b Leis Wl Lat from L, below, p. 493; f. 59 CHn cor (cf. below, West), below, p. 521; f. 59v.—69 laws of the 13th century; f. 70 Registrum brevium; f. 75 Heptarchy, episcopal sees, political districts *De longitudine . . Anglie.

F. 77 *In Cn, below, p. 612; f. 84 *Chnutus rex cum XX annis, i.e. Huntingdon3, by which S too takes its place in the class Ip Hunt (above, p. xxxi). There follows from Tripartita: f. 84 *Wl art, below, p. 486; f. 84b *Geneal. Normannica usque II Henricum, continued to John.

F. 86b blank; f. 87—98b laws of the 13th century.

S was copied in Vl and Harley 785.

notes.text_de: vgl. mein Über Leges Ed. Conf. S. 126. 130.
notes.text_en: cf. my Über Leges Ed. Conf. pp. 126. 130.

transcription.doubts: Here 'Geneal. Normannica' is in roman, only 'usque II Henricum,' in italic. 'Tripartita' is bold (hyphenated Tri-partita across a line).

others.text: O’Brien (2003): late 13th century. With Lb, the manuscript whose readings Liebermann reports least reliably (see Lb); he missed, e.g., S’s montam and feldchirche at I 3,2. O’Brien’s family tree puts S beside a lost manuscript (π) from which Pl and the two 16th-century transcripts Vincent 98 and Harley 785 descend; on this view Harley 785 is not a copy of S.
